output.headline: Extends the state refugee student grant to June 2021; no new money is added
output.summary: This amendment to a California Department of Social Services grant extends the time to use the money from June 20, 2020 to June 13, 2021. The district uses the unspent part of the $1,835,520 grant to serve newcomer refugee and unaccompanied minor students. The text states no added dollars.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $58,800 for Legacy Leaders to supply an interim principal at Sankofa Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $58,800.00

output.summary: The district contracted with Legacy Leaders, LLC to supply an interim principal at Sankofa Academy for December 2, 2019 through May 29, 2020, for no more than $58,800. The service began before the board's approval, which is a ratification.

output.headline: Proclaims April 20-24, 2020 as Oakland Adult and Career Education Week
output.summary: This resolution proclaims April 20-24, 2020 as Oakland Adult and Career Education Week in the district. The item lists no fiscal impact.

output.headline: Awards $195,000 to Bay City Engineering to replace the boilers at Sankofa Academy
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title names the contractor 'Bay City Boiler & Engineering Co., Inc.' while the action text names 'Bay City Engineering Company, Inc.'.
output.summary: The district chose Bay City Engineering Company as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder to remove the old boiler and install two new cast-iron boilers at Sankofa Academy. Work is scheduled to start April 8, 2020 and last 90 calendar days, ending July 7, 2020. The contract went through competitive bidding.

output.headline: Ratifies $2,250 for Blue Thistle Consulting to document the Kindergarten Readiness Program

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $2,250.00

output.summary: Blue Thistle Consulting will write a workflow and transition timeline document for the Kindergarten Readiness Program, covering its responsibilities, structure, timeline and partnerships, because the program manager is leaving. The contract runs February 18 through June 30, 2020, for no more than $2,250. It began before the board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies $6,500 for Mills Teacher Scholars to run a planning retreat for Expanded Learning staff

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $6,500.00

output.summary: Mills Teacher Scholars facilitated a two-day strategic planning retreat for the district's Expanded Learning staff on February 10 and 11 at Mills College. It also helped set the agenda beforehand and reflected with the team afterward, for no more than $6,500. The work began before the board's approval.

output.headline: Awards $265,000 to Bay City Engineering to replace the boilers at Melrose Leadership Academy
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title names the contractor 'Bay City Boiler & Engineering Co., Inc.' while the action text names 'Bay City Engineering Company, Inc.'.
output.summary: The district chose Bay City Engineering Company as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder to remove the old boiler and install two new cast-iron boilers at Melrose Leadership Academy. The $265,000 includes a $30,000 contingency allowance. Work is scheduled to start April 8, 2020 and end July 7, 2020.

output.headline: Adds $12,771 to the inspector contract for the Emerson Elementary softball field, now $52,371
output.summary: This amendment adds inspection work with Anthonio, Inc. on the Emerson Elementary School Softball Field Project. The state architect's office (Division of the State Architect) requires a higher class of inspector of record than the drawings showed. It adds $12,771, including a $6,831 contingency allowance, raising the cap from $39,600 to $52,371, and extends the term to December 3, 2020.

output.headline: Awards $135,000 to Bay Construction Company to replace the storm drain at Sherman Campus
output.summary: The district chose Bay Construction Company as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder to remove damaged asphalt, dig a trench and install a new drainage system at the Sherman Campus. Work is scheduled to start April 8, 2020 and last 90 calendar days, ending July 7, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts a $50,000 state grant for Skyline High's Renewable Energy Academy
output.summary: The district accepts a $50,000 California Partnerships Academies career technical education grant from the California Department of Education for the Skyline High School Renewable Energy Academy. The grant period is March 1, 2020 through March 1, 2021.

output.headline: Accepts a $50,000 state grant for Castlemont High's Sustainable Urban Design Academy
output.summary: The district accepts a $50,000 California Partnerships Academies career technical education grant from the California Department of Education for the Sustainable Urban Design Academy at Castlemont High School. The grant period is March 1, 2020 through March 1, 2021.

output.headline: Awards $220,000 to Bay Construction Company to replace the sewer line at Elmhurst Middle
output.summary: The district chose Bay Construction Company as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder to repair and replace the 6-inch sewer main from the main building and portables to the city street, and to replace concrete and asphalt affected by the work. Work is scheduled to start April 8, 2020 and end July 7, 2020.

output.headline: Ratifies $24,800 more for TeachBar's teacher-exam test prep and tutoring, now $62,776
output.summary: This amendment adds $24,800 to the contract with TeachBar for test preparation and tutoring that helps teacher candidates pass California teacher certification exams. It raises the contract cap from $37,976 to $62,776 for August 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020. The board is approving it after the contract period began.

output.headline: Leases part of the Lakeview site to American Indian Public High School for about $151,100
output.summary: The district lets American Indian Public High School, a charter school, use part of the Lakeview School Site at 746 Grand Ave. to run grades 9-12 from July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021. This is an in-lieu of Proposition 39 agreement, and the school pays the district an anticipated use fee of $151,099.72.

output.headline: Approves layoffs and additions of classified positions for the 2020-21 school year
output.summary: This resolution reduces or lays off some classified (non-teaching) positions and adds or creates others for fiscal year 2020-2021, based on lack of funds or program need. It follows an earlier resolution from March 4, 2020 and the 2020-2021 budget development process. The text gives no dollar amounts or position counts.
